props.title: A few lines are enough.
body: The most useful message says who the system is for, what it has to hold, and where the current approach hurts. It does not need to be formal or complete.
If you are not sure which type fits, pick the closest. The conversation can find its own shape.

items.q: Can a block hold another block?
a: No. Blocks sit one after another. A signature block can host a richer composition of its own, but blocks do not nest.
A closer. Every page except the contact page and the site map finishes with its own composition, and no two pages share one. None of them is a call to action.
A composition that belongs to one page: a find bar for a long document, a tool, a demonstration. It is loaded when the page needs it, and it holds its height while it loads so that nothing jumps.

items.q: How do I add a new kind of block?
a: Write a component in the blocks folder, add one line to the block list so the loader knows its type, and add it to the catalogue on this page. If it brings keys that are not prose, add them to the search engine’s skip list.

items.q: Is the text in the component or in the data?
a: In the data. A component decides how things look and move; the words belong to the page.

props.title: A callout is for one thing.
props.heading: Use it sparingly
body: Use a callout for the single remark a reader must not miss: an honest limit, an open question, a warning. If every paragraph is a callout, none of them is read.
The kind of remark is written out as a word as well as shown by colour and icon, so it never depends on colour alone.

props.title: How a block gets onto a page.
props.intro: In order, with no dates, because the order is what matters.

items.title: Write the data
items.body: Add an object to the page’s list of blocks in its data file. Everything the reader will see is in it.

items.title: Give it a type
items.body: The type names the block. The page loader looks the type up and draws it.

items.title: Choose a scene
items.body: A Canvas scene is drawn behind the block. Blocks that carry text use the calmest scenes.

items.title: Check it
items.body: Run the page-ending, smoke, contrast and accessibility checks. A block is not finished until they pass.

columns.title: Start here
items: The content is text, records or links
A standard layout does the job
The kit already has the component

columns.label: Signature
columns.title: When the page is the interaction
items: The point of the page is something you do
The data has a shape no other page shares
The layout is part of the idea
It would not make sense anywhere else

props.verdict: Start with a generic block. Reach for a signature when the page’s point is something a reader does and not something a reader reads.

tabs.label: Scene
body: Every block can name a Canvas scene and how intense it should be. The scene is drawn behind the block and pauses off screen.
Blocks that carry a lot of text use the calmest scenes, and a measurement script keeps them calm.

tabs.label: Anchor
body: An anchor gives a block an address on its page, so a link can point at it. A rail label puts it on the side rail that follows the reader down the page.

tabs.label: Motion
body: Each block reveals itself as it enters the screen. Under reduced motion it is simply there, and the animated backgrounds hold a single frame.

props.quote: Movement carries meaning — state, direction, hierarchy. Nothing moves to decorate.
props.cite: Hanoryx Systems · Principle 03, Motion with purpose
props.context: A quote block is for words someone really said and agreed to have quoted. This site uses it for its own principles, never for testimonials.
